name: Haste Magic
oracle_text: Target creature gets +3/+1 and gains haste until end of turn. Exile the top card of your library. You may play it until your next end step.
blocked_sentences: You may play it until your next end step.

needs.what: an impulse-exile permission whose clock is a duration rather than the current turn -- here specifically 'until your next end step', which when the spell is cast on an opponent's turn spans the rest of that turn, every other player's turn, and your following turn up to its end step. `exile`'s `playable_this_turn` (and `grant_playable`, which carries no duration at all) needs to accept a duration form -- e.g. `playable: "until_your_next_end_step"` / `until_your_next_turn` -- and every consumer of the permission must honour the recorded expiry instead of comparing against the current turn number.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `exile` carries only the boolean `playable_this_turn`, and `look_at_top`'s `playable_this_turn` is the same single-turn flag; `grant_playable` takes `any_type`, `limit` and `objects` and no `duration` at all. Shipping `playable_this_turn` would be an approximation in the *narrowing* direction: cast on an opponent's turn (this is an Instant, so that is a normal line of play) the printed card lets you play the exiled card right through your next turn up to your end step, while `playable_this_turn` revokes it at the turn boundary -- a strictly WORSE card than printed, which fails the fidelity rule just as surely as the more usual strictly-better error, and fails it silently since nothing on the board shows the permission expiring early. Going the other way, `grant_playable` with no duration is an open-ended permission and is strictly better than printed. `play_exiled` is a different effect (cast now, for free, not a deferred permission at the printed price). `delay`/`delayed_trigger` cannot re-grant the permission later either: bindings live for one resolution, and `exiled_with` reads `exiled_by`, which `exile` only sets under `link`/`until_leaves` -- flags that mean 'return it', not 'it is still playable'. The engine already expresses `until_your_next_turn` for detain/goad/cant_block, so the clock is representable; it has simply never been wired to the impulse permission. This is the same engine gap already recorded for Light Up the Stage.

notes: The rest of the card is expressible and is not blocked: 'Target creature gets +3/+1 and gains haste until end of turn.' is a card-level target of kind creature plus `pump` (power 3, toughness 1) and `grant_keyword` (keyword haste, duration until_end_of_turn) on that target, and 'Exile the top card of your library.' is `exile` against the top card of your library. Only the permission's duration blocks the card, so per the brief no partial answer was written.
